chunks: Ibn Mahbub from Ibn Ri'ab from Abu Basir said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a Muslim man who died, leaving behind a Christian mother, a wife, and Muslim children. He said, 'If his mother converts to Islam before his inheritance is distributed, she is given one-sixth.'

I said, 'And if he had no wife, no children, and no heir with a prescribed share in the Book from among the Muslims, and his mother was Christian, and he had Christian relatives who would have a prescribed share in the Book if they were Muslims, then to whom would his inheritance belong?'

He said, 'If his mother converts, then all his inheritance belongs to her. And if his mother does not convert, but some of his relatives convert who have a prescribed share in the Book, then the inheritance belongs to them. And if none of his relatives convert, then the inheritance belongs to the Imam.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to the inheritance of a Muslim man if his Christian mother converts after his death but before distribution?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the principle of *al-walaya* (guardianship) in Shia jurisprudence, where the Imam serves as the ultimate heir (*al-imam warith*) when no Muslim relatives with prescribed shares exist. It highlights the critical condition of the mother's conversion prior to estate distribution, demonstrating how her status shifts from a non-Muslim relative to a primary heir, thereby excluding other non-Muslim kin. This ruling underscores the Shia view that non-Muslims do not inherit from Muslims unless they possess a specific prescribed share, and their absence leaves the estate to the Imam.
